message.content: {"outcome":"DIRECT_SUB_OPTIMAL","best_model_id":"PGS003972","confidence":"Moderate","rationale":"All 6 candidates are direct matches (trait_reported/trait_efo and phenotyping_reported all indicate abdominal aortic aneurysm, with one explicitly prevalent AAA). Among them, PGS003972 is preferred because it comes from a disease-focused GWAS meta-analysis publication (Nat Genet AAA meta-analysis with many contributing cohorts) and uses a genome-wide shrinkage method (PRS-CS), which domain guidance favors over pan-trait/framework-derived scores when endpoint fidelity is comparable. Competing options have notable limitations: PGS001784 (Cell Genom “Global Biobank analyses…”) and PGS002054 (Am J Hum Genet “Portability of 245 polygenic scores…”) are framework/portability-style scores; PGS000753 is an older sparse P+T score with prevalent-case phenotype and no AUC/R2; and PGS003429 is from a screening/cost-effectiveness framing with unknown covariates and only a full-model AUROC reported. Confidence is not high because performance reporting is not clearly PRS-only/comparable across candidates (e.g., high full-model metrics like C-index 0.882 for PGS003973 may be covariate-driven; PGS003972 shows only full-model AUROC 0.69; several lack PRS-only AUC/R2), and the two Nat Genet scores (PGS003972 vs PGS003973) are difficult to separate cleanly from the provided metadata alone."}

{"outcome":"DIRECT_SUB_OPTIMAL","best_model_id":"PGS000753","confidence":"Moderate","rationale":"All 6 candidates are direct matches by trait_reported/trait_efo and have phenotype labels consistent with abdominal aortic aneurysm (AAA). Several models (PGS001784, PGS002054) come from explicit portability/pan-trait framework papers, which domain guidance says to down-rank when disease-focused alternatives exist. Among the disease-focused options, PGS000753 (MVP/MAYO-VDB AAA study in Circulation) has clean endpoint wording (prevalent AAA), basic covariates (age/sex/PCs), and a reasonably large external validation sample (n=46,564), plus an explicit per-SD effect size (OR 1.37, 95% CI 1.30–1.44) supporting meaningful PRS signal. Competing disease-focused newer candidates (PGS003972/PGS003973; Nat Genet AAA meta-analysis) have broader multi-cohort development but provide only full-model discrimination metrics (AUROC/C-index) with limited/unknown covariate detail and small validation sizes (~7k), making their reported high C-index (0.882) difficult to interpret as PRS contribution per the domain rules. Because performance metrics are inconsistently reported across models (often full-model only vs PRS-only/partial metrics) and key covariate information is missing for some, the selection remains sub-optimal rather than clearly high-quality."}

{"outcome":"DIRECT_SUB_OPTIMAL","best_model_id":"PGS003972","confidence":"Moderate","rationale":"All 6 candidates are direct matches by trait_reported/trait_efo and have endpoint-faithful phenotyping_reported (abdominal aortic aneurysm or prevalent AAA). Several are framework/portability-style scores (PGS001784: Global Biobank analyses; PGS002054: UKB portability paper), which domain guidance says should generally not outrank a disease-focused multi-cohort AAA study unless they show clearly superior, PRS-comparable evidence. Among the disease-focused Nat Genet AAA meta-analysis scores (PGS003972/PGS003973), PGS003972 is preferred because it comes from a clearly disease-focused multi-cohort development (many AAA cohorts listed) and reports a discrimination metric (AUROC=0.69) without any indication of heavy clinical covariate packaging (covariates are ‘Unknown’ rather than explicitly biomarker/comorbidity-heavy). PGS003973 reports a higher C-index (0.882) but includes age and sex covariates and provides only full-model discrimination without PRS-only/incremental metrics, making comparability unclear per the domain rules; the very high value could be largely covariate-driven. Remaining limitation: performance reporting is not cleanly comparable across candidates (some provide PRS-only R2/partial-r, others only full-model AUROC/C-index, and covariates are missing/unknown for key models), so the choice is not decisively supported, lowering the outcome to DIRECT_SUB_OPTIMAL and confidence to Moderate."}

{"outcome":"DIRECT_SUB_OPTIMAL","best_model_id":"PGS003972","confidence":"Moderate","rationale":"All 6 candidates are direct matches (trait_reported/trait_efo and phenotyping_reported all align to abdominal aortic aneurysm, with one explicitly prevalent AAA for PGS000753). Among them, PGS003972 (Nat Genet 2023 AAA GWAS meta-analysis) is best supported by study archetype: it is disease-focused and multi-cohort (many contributing cohorts listed) rather than a pan-trait/framework score, and it uses a genome-wide shrinkage method (PRS-CS) with EUR evaluation. However, the performance evidence is limited/less comparable across candidates: several models report only full-model AUROC/C-index (e.g., PGS003972 AUROC=0.69; PGS003973 C-index=0.882) and covariates are unknown for some (including PGS003972), while others come from framework/portability papers with PRS-only/adjusted metrics but weaker study focus (e.g., PGS001784 from a global biobank framework; PGS002054 from a UKB portability study). Given these comparability gaps (especially unclear covariates and mixed metric types), the selection is not strongly decisive, so confidence is Moderate and the overall outcome is DIRECT_SUB_OPTIMAL."}

{"outcome":"DIRECT_HIGH_QUALITY","best_model_id":"PGS003972","confidence":"Moderate","rationale":"All 6 candidates are direct matches (trait_reported/trait_efo and phenotyping_reported consistently indicate abdominal aortic aneurysm, without horizon-conditioned or risk-wrapper packaging). Among them, PGS003972 is best supported by a disease-focused, multi-cohort AAA GWAS meta-analysis context (Nat Genet; many contributing cohorts listed) using a genome-wide shrinkage method (PRS-CS) with European evaluation, which aligns with the domain guidance favoring disease-focused multi-cohort scores over pan-trait/portability frameworks. {"outcome":"DIRECT_SUB_OPTIMAL","best_model_id":"PGS003972","confidence":"Moderate","rationale":"All 6 candidates are direct matches on trait_reported/trait_efo and have phenotype fields consistent with AAA (one is explicitly prevalent AAA but still endpoint-faithful for a generic AAA target). Several candidates are from pan-trait/framework-style papers (PGS001784: Global Biobank analyses; PGS002054: Portability of 245 polygenic scores) which domain guidance says should not outrank a disease-focused multi-cohort AAA score unless they have clearly cleaner endpoint/metric evidence. Among disease-focused candidates, PGS003972 and PGS003973 come from a dedicated AAA GWAS meta-analysis (Nat Genet, multi-cohort development) and use genome-wide PRS-CS with European evaluation; this disease-focused multi-cohort context is the strongest endpoint/study-design signal in the set. Between those two, PGS003972 has the broader, more externally oriented validation context visible (record_count=3 vs 1) and reports a standard discrimination metric (AUROC=0.69), whereas PGS003973 reports a higher C-index (0.882) but the context suggests this is likely a covariate-influenced full-model metric (age/age^2/sex) and is not directly comparable to PRS-only performance; relying on it would conflict with the policy not to substitute full-model discrimination for PRS evidence. Key limitation: none of the candidates provides clearly comparable PRS-only AUROC across the set, several have missing/unknown covariates, and PGS003972’s reported AUROC is modest with small validation size, so the choice is supported mainly by study archetype/endpoint fidelity rather than decisive, comparable PRS-only performance."}

{"outcome":"DIRECT_SUB_OPTIMAL","best_model_id":"PGS003972","confidence":"Moderate","rationale":"All 6 candidates are direct matches (trait_reported/trait_efo and phenotyping_reported explicitly indicate abdominal aortic aneurysm). Several are from pan-trait/framework or portability contexts (PGS001784: Global Biobank framework; PGS002054: UKB portability study), which the provided domain policy says to down-rank when a disease-focused multi-cohort alternative exists. Two candidates (PGS003972/PGS003973) come from a disease-focused AAA GWAS meta-analysis (Nat Genet 2023) with broad multi-cohort development, which is supportive for endpoint fidelity and study archetype. Between these two, PGS003972 is preferred because it avoids potential non-comparability from stronger clinical covariate packaging and metric interpretation ambiguity: PGS003973 reports only a full-model C-index (0.882) with age/age^2/sex and no PRS-only/incremental metric, whereas PGS003972 reports a more modest full-model AUROC (0.69) but similarly lacks PRS-only metrics; choosing the lower, less outlier-like full-model metric reduces risk of over-weighting covariate-driven discrimination per the domain guidance. Confidence is only Moderate because key PRS-comparable performance (PGS-only AUROC/incremental AUROC) is missing across the leading disease-focused candidates, and several other direct-match models have much larger validation samples (e.g., PGS001784) albeit in framework contexts."}

{"outcome":"DIRECT_SUB_OPTIMAL","best_model_id":"PGS003972","confidence":"Moderate","rationale":"All 6 candidates are direct matches (trait_reported/trait_efo and phenotyping_reported are abdominal aortic aneurysm or prevalent AAA). However, the evidence is not sufficient to identify a single clearly best model without caveats because performance reporting is heterogeneous and often not PRS-comparable: several models provide only full-model AUROC/C-index with unknown covariates (PGS003429, PGS003972), while others are from known pan-trait/framework contexts where reported metrics may not reflect disease-optimized PRS development (PGS001784: Global Biobank framework; PGS002054: UKB portability framework). Among disease-focused options, PGS003972 (Nat Genet AAA GWAS meta-analysis) offers a coherent, disease-specific multi-cohort development set (many AAA-relevant cohorts listed) and an endpoint-aligned phenotype; its reported full-model AUROC=0.69 is modest but does not appear driven by disclosed heavy clinical covariates (covariates listed as Unknown). The presence of a very high C-index for PGS003973 (0.882) is not used as decisive because it likely reflects covariate-including survival/discrimination (Age, Age^2, Sex) rather than an explicitly PRS-only metric, so it is not directly comparable to other candidates’ PRS contribution. Overall, PGS003972 is preferred on endpoint fidelity plus disease-focused multi-cohort context, but the lack of clearly PRS-only performance metrics and unknown covariates prevent a high-confidence selection."}

{"outcome":"DIRECT_SUB_OPTIMAL","best_model_id":"PGS003973","confidence":"Moderate","rationale":"All 6 candidates are direct matches (trait_reported/trait_efo and phenotyping_reported align to abdominal aortic aneurysm), so selection hinges on comparative support.
